category: PyAEDT: Reports, Solution Data, Field Plots, Far Fields & Data Export
description: The hfss.post PostProcessor3D object and the classes it hands out: typed report builders by category, the Standard/FarField report objects with their traces, markers, limit lines and axis editing, SolutionData for numeric access and plotting, field plots on surfaces/volumes/cut planes/lines and their PyVista rendering, field-file exports, the Fields Calculator wrapper and expression builder, model pictures and mesh export, antenna far-field data (FfdSolutionData), monostatic RCS export and Touchstone post-processing.

tools.name: hfss.post.reports_by_category.standard / far_field / fields / near_field / antenna_parameters / modal_solution / terminal_solution / eigenmode / emission / spectral
tools.description: Typed report factories that return an unsaved report object of the right class for a category, with the category-specific properties exposed (far_field_sphere for far fields, polyline for fields, source context for antenna parameters). The object is configured through attributes - expressions, primary_sweep, variations, report_type, domain - and then create() adds it to AEDT; this is the more controllable alternative to the one-shot post.create_report.
tools.usage:
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.standard(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.far_field(expressions=None, setup=None, sphere_name=None, source_context=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.fields(expressions=None, setup=None, polyline=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.near_field(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.antenna_parameters(expressions=None, setup=None, infinite_sphere=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.modal_solution(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.terminal_solution(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.eigenmode(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.emission(expressions=None, setup=None)
rep.create(name=None)

parameters.name: expressions
parameters.description: String or list of report expressions for the category.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" or "Setup1 : LastAdaptive" (hfss.nominal_sweep / nominal_adaptive).

parameters.name: sphere_name / infinite_sphere
parameters.description: Infinite sphere used as context for far-field and antenna-parameter reports.

parameters.name: polyline
parameters.description: Polyline name giving the Fields report its distance sweep.

parameters.name: rep.report_type
parameters.description: Display type: "Rectangular Plot", "Polar Plot", "3D Polar Plot", "Smith Chart", "Data Table", "Radiation Pattern", "Rectangular Contour Plot", "Rectangular Stacked Plot".

tools.example:
ff = hfss.post.reports_by_category.far_field("dB(RealizedGainTotal)", hfss.nominal_adaptive, sphere_name="3D")
ff.variations = {"Freq": ["2.45GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["0deg", "90deg"]}
ff.primary_sweep = "Theta"
ff.report_type = "Radiation Pattern"
ff.create("Gain cuts")

fld = hfss.post.reports_by_category.fields("Mag_E", hfss.nominal_adaptive, polyline="Probe")
fld.variations = {"Freq": ["2.45GHz"], "Phase": ["0deg"], "Distance": ["All"]}
fld.create("E along probe")

ap = hfss.post.reports_by_category.antenna_parameters("PeakRealizedGain", hfss.nominal_adaptive, infinite_sphere="3D")
ap.report_type = "Data Table"
ap.create()
tools.notes: Available categories depend on the solution type (hfss.post.available_report_types). The report object's traces property lists the traces after creation; hfss.post.plots holds all report objects of the design.

tools.name: Standard report object (expressions, primary_sweep, variations, domain, report_type, create, traces)
tools.description: The class behind every 2D/3D report created by PyAEDT (returned by post.create_report and the reports_by_category factories). Its properties mirror the Modify Report dialog - expressions, primary and secondary sweep, variations (families), domain (Sweep/Time), report_category, report_type, plot_name - and after create() it owns the traces, limit lines and notes in the plot. Reports are created in AEDT by name and can be re-fetched later from hfss.post.plots.
tools.usage:
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.standard(["dB(S(1,1))", "dB(S(2,1))"], hfss.nominal_sweep)
rep.expressions / rep.primary_sweep / rep.secondary_sweep / rep.variations / rep.domain
rep.report_category / rep.report_type / rep.plot_name / rep.setup
rep.create(name=None)
rep.traces / rep.limit_lines / rep.notes / rep.internal_plot_name
rep.get_solution_data()
rep.update_expressions_with_defaults(quantities_category=None)
rep.delete()

parameters.name: expressions
parameters.description: List of Y expressions; each becomes a trace.

parameters.name: primary_sweep / secondary_sweep
parameters.description: X axis variable ("Freq", "Time", "Theta", "Phi", "Distance" or a design variable) and the second axis for 3D/contour plots.

parameters.name: variations
parameters.description: Dict {variable: [values]} - "All" or explicit values; a variable with several values produces a family of traces.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: "Sweep" (frequency) or "Time".

parameters.name: update_expressions_with_defaults
parameters.description: Fill expressions with all quantities of a category (e.g. every S-parameter).

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.reports_by_category.standard(["dB(S(1,1))", "dB(S(2,1))"], hfss.nominal_sweep)
rep.variations = {"Freq": ["All"], "patch_l": ["27mm", "29mm", "31mm"]}
rep.primary_sweep = "Freq"
rep.report_type = "Rectangular Plot"
rep.create("S vs length")
print(rep.traces)
data = rep.get_solution_data()
print(data.primary_sweep_values[:5])

# 3D contour: S11 versus frequency and patch length
rep2 = hfss.post.reports_by_category.standard("dB(S(1,1))", hfss.nominal_sweep)
rep2.variations = {"Freq": ["All"], "patch_l": ["All"]}
rep2.primary_sweep = "Freq"; rep2.secondary_sweep = "patch_l"
rep2.report_type = "Rectangular Contour Plot"
rep2.create("S11 map")
tools.notes: Native: oModule("ReportSetup").CreateReport(name, "Modal Solution Data", "Rectangular Plot", "Setup1 : Sweep1", ["Domain:=", "Sweep"], ["Freq:=", ["All"], "patch_l:=", ["27mm", "29mm"]], ["X Component:=", "Freq", "Y Component:=", ["dB(S(1,1))"]]). Report names must be unique in the design; create() renames on clash.

tools.name: report.add_trace_to_report / update_trace_in_report / delete_traces / import_traces
tools.description: Trace management on an existing report: append expressions as new traces (optionally with their own setup, variations and sweep), update existing traces with new settings, delete traces by name, and import traces from a CSV/TAB/DAT file (measured data overlaid on simulation). These replace the right-click > Add Trace / Modify Report / Import workflow.
tools.usage:
rep.add_trace_to_report(traces, setup_name=None, variations=None, context=None)
rep.update_trace_in_report(traces, setup_name=None, variations=None, context=None)
rep.delete_traces(plot_name, traces_list)
rep.import_traces(input_file, plot_name)
rep.add_trace_characteristics(name, arguments=None, solution_range=None)

parameters.name: traces
parameters.description: Expression or list of expressions.

parameters.name: setup_name / variations / context
parameters.description: Override the report's defaults for the added traces.

parameters.name: traces_list
parameters.description: Trace names as shown in rep.traces (expression plus variation suffix).

parameters.name: input_file
parameters.description: .csv, .tab or .dat with a header line naming the columns.

parameters.name: add_trace_characteristics
parameters.description: Add a trace characteristic (e.g. "XAtYVal", "max", "BandwidthAtYVal") with its arguments to the plot's characteristics table.

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.create_report("dB(S(1,1))")
rep.add_trace_to_report("dB(S(2,1))")
rep.import_traces("C:/meas/vna_s11.csv", rep.plot_name)
rep.add_trace_characteristics("XAtYVal", arguments=["-10"], solution_range=["Full"])
rep.delete_traces(rep.plot_name, [rep.traces[-1]])
tools.notes: Native: oModule.AddTraces(report, solution, context, families, data), oModule.UpdateTraces, oModule.DeleteTraces([report], [traces]), oModule.ImportIntoReport(report, file). Imported traces carry no variations and cannot be re-solved.

tools.name: report.add_limit_line_from_points / add_limit_line_from_equation / add_cartesian_x_marker / add_cartesian_y_marker / add_note
tools.description: Annotations on a 2D report: limit lines from x/y point lists or from an equation over a range (specification masks for return loss, isolation, emissions), Cartesian markers at fixed X or Y values, and text notes at a position. Combined with export_report_to_jpg they produce spec-check figures for reports directly from the script.
tools.usage:
rep.add_limit_line_from_points(x_list, y_list, x_units="", y_units="", y_axis="Y1")
rep.add_limit_line_from_equation(start_x, stop_x, step, equation="x", units="GHz", y_axis=1)
rep.add_cartesian_x_marker(value, name=None)
rep.add_cartesian_y_marker(value, name=None, y_axis=1)
rep.add_note(text, x_position=2000, y_position=2000)
rep.limit_lines / rep.notes

parameters.name: x_list / y_list
parameters.description: Point coordinates of the mask; units strings apply to both lists.

parameters.name: equation / start_x / stop_x / step
parameters.description: Expression in x evaluated over the range.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Marker position with units, e.g. "2.45GHz" or "-10".

parameters.name: x_position / y_position
parameters.description: Note anchor in plot pixel units.

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.create_report("dB(S(1,1))")
rep.add_limit_line_from_points([2.4, 2.4, 2.5, 2.5], [0, -10, -10, 0], x_units="GHz", y_units="dB")
rep.add_cartesian_x_marker("2.45GHz", name="f0")
rep.add_cartesian_y_marker("-10", name="spec")
rep.add_note("Return loss spec: -10 dB over 2.4-2.5 GHz", x_position=1500, y_position=3000)
hfss.post.export_report_to_jpg(hfss.working_directory, rep.plot_name)
tools.notes: Limit lines are static (they do not follow variations) and are stored with the report. Native: oModule.AddCartesianLimitLine(...), AddCartesianXMarker, AddCartesianYMarker, AddNote through ChangeProperty of the report.

tools.name: report.edit_x_axis / edit_y_axis / edit_x_axis_scaling / edit_y_axis_scaling / edit_grid / edit_legend / edit_general_settings / edit_header / hide_legend
tools.description: Formatting of a 2D report from Python: axis fonts, labels and colours, axis scaling (linear/log, min/max, auto), grid style, legend content and position, general appearance (background, plot area colours), the header/title block and legend visibility. They wrap the report's ChangeProperty calls so plots exported for documentation look consistent without touching the GUI.
tools.usage:
rep.edit_x_axis(font="Arial", font_size=12, italic=False, bold=False, color=(0, 0, 0), label="")
rep.edit_y_axis(name="Y1", font="Arial", font_size=12, italic=False, bold=False, color=(0, 0, 0), label="")
rep.edit_x_axis_scaling(linear_scaling=True, min_scale=None, max_scale=None, minor_tick_divs=5, min_spacing=None, units=None)
rep.edit_y_axis_scaling(name="Y1", linear_scaling=True, min_scale=None, max_scale=None, minor_tick_divs=5, min_spacing=None, units=None)
rep.edit_grid(minor_x=True, minor_y=True, major_x=True, major_y=True, style_minor="Solid", style_major="Solid", minor_color=(0,0,0), major_color=(0,0,0))
rep.edit_legend(show_solution_name=True, show_variation_key=True, show_trace_name=True, back_color=(255,255,255), font="Arial", font_size=9, ...)
rep.edit_general_settings(background_color=(255,255,255), plot_color=(255,255,255), enable_y_stripes=True, field_width=4, precision=4, use_scientific_notation=True)
rep.edit_header(company_name="", show_design_name=True, font="Arial", title_size=12, subtitle_size=12, ...)
rep.hide_legend(solution_name=True, trace_name=True, variation_key=True, font_height=100)

parameters.name: min_scale / max_scale / units
parameters.description: Fixed axis range and units (e.g. "GHz"); None keeps auto scaling.

parameters.name: linear_scaling
parameters.description: False switches the axis to logarithmic.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Axis label text; empty keeps the automatic label.

parameters.name: name (Y axis)
parameters.description: "Y1", "Y2"... for stacked/secondary axes.

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.create_report(["dB(S(1,1))", "dB(S(2,1))"])
rep.edit_x_axis_scaling(min_scale="1GHz", max_scale="6GHz", units="GHz")
rep.edit_y_axis_scaling(min_scale="-40", max_scale="0")
rep.edit_x_axis(font_size=14, label="Frequency")
rep.edit_y_axis(font_size=14, label="S-parameters (dB)")
rep.edit_grid(minor_x=False, minor_y=False)
rep.edit_legend(show_solution_name=False, show_variation_key=False)
rep.edit_header(company_name="RF Lab", show_design_name=True)
tools.notes: All of these map to oModule("ReportSetup").ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:Axis" / "Legend" / "General" / "Header" ..., ["NAME:PropServers", "<plot>:AxisX"], ["NAME:ChangedProps", ...]]]). Default report appearance for new plots is set in Tools > Options > Report2D options.

tools.name: report.export_config / hfss.post.create_report_from_configuration / report.apply_report_template
tools.description: Report templates in PyAEDT form: export_config writes a report's full definition (expressions, context, variations, formatting, limit lines) to a JSON file, create_report_from_configuration rebuilds a report from such a JSON/TOML, from an AEDT .rpt template or from a dictionary against any solution, and apply_report_template applies an .rpt template file to an existing report. This is how a standard set of plots is reproduced on every design of a project family.
tools.usage:
rep.export_config(output_file)
rep = hfss.post.create_report_from_configuration(input_file=None, report_settings=None, solution_name=None, name=None,
                                                 matplotlib=False, show=True, hide_legend=False, snapshot_path=None, width=800, height=450)
rep.apply_report_template(input_file, property_type="Graphical")

parameters.name: output_file / input_file
parameters.description: .json or .toml (PyAEDT format) or .rpt (AEDT template exported with Save As Report Template).

parameters.name: report_settings
parameters.description: Dictionary with the same structure as the JSON (read_json / read_toml helpers).

parameters.name: solution_name
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" to apply the template to; None keeps the one in the file.

parameters.name: matplotlib / snapshot_path
parameters.description: Render with the PyAEDT ReportPlotter instead of AEDT and/or save an image.

parameters.name: property_type
parameters.description: "Graphical", "Data" or "All" - which parts of the .rpt template to apply.

tools.example:
rep = hfss.post.create_report(["dB(S(1,1))", "dB(S(2,1))"])
rep.edit_y_axis_scaling(min_scale="-40", max_scale="0")
rep.export_config("C:/templates/sparam_report.json")

other = Hfss(project="C:/work/filter_v2.aedt")
other.post.create_report_from_configuration("C:/templates/sparam_report.json", solution_name="Setup1 : Sweep1")
other.post.create_report_from_configuration("C:/templates/aedt_template.rpt")
tools.notes: Native: oModule.CreateReportFromTemplate(path) and SaveReportAsTemplate(report, path) for .rpt files; the JSON path is PyAEDT-only. The PyAEDT 'Generate Report' extension uses these JSON files to build PDF reports.

tools.name: FarField report object (far_field_sphere, source_context, primary_sweep_range, display_families_type)
tools.description: The report class for the Far Fields category returned by reports_by_category.far_field. Besides the Standard properties it carries the infinite-sphere context (far_field_sphere), the array/source context for component arrays, primary and secondary sweep ranges (to restrict Theta/Phi without listing values) and the families display type. Radiation Pattern (polar) and 3D Polar plot types are selected through report_type.
tools.usage:
ff = hfss.post.reports_by_category.far_field("dB(GainTotal)", hfss.nominal_adaptive, sphere_name="3D")
ff.far_field_sphere = "3D"
ff.primary_sweep = "Theta"; ff.secondary_sweep = "Phi"
ff.primary_sweep_range = ["-180deg", "180deg"]
ff.variations = {"Freq": ["2.45GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["All"]}
ff.report_type = "3D Polar Plot"      # or "Radiation Pattern", "Rectangular Plot", "Data Table"
ff.create("Gain3D")

parameters.name: far_field_sphere
parameters.description: Name of the infinite sphere setup that defines the angular grid and coordinate system.

parameters.name: source_context / source_group
parameters.description: For component arrays: which array/source context the pattern is computed for.

parameters.name: primary_sweep_range / secondary_sweep_range
parameters.description: [start, stop] limits for the angular sweeps.

parameters.name: display_families_type
parameters.description: How families are displayed for reports with X and Y components.

tools.example:
ff = hfss.post.reports_by_category.far_field(["dB(GainTheta)", "dB(GainPhi)"], hfss.nominal_adaptive, sphere_name="3D")
ff.variations = {"Freq": ["10GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["0deg", "90deg"]}
ff.primary_sweep = "Theta"
ff.report_type = "Radiation Pattern"
ff.create("E and H plane cuts")
hfss.post.export_report_to_csv(hfss.working_directory, "E and H plane cuts")
tools.notes: Native context array for far fields: ["Context:=", "3D"] plus ["Domain:=", "Sweep"]; for arrays ["Context:=", "3D", "SourceContext:=", ...]. Far-field quantities include GainTotal/Theta/Phi/LHCP/RHCP/X/Y/L3X/L3Y, RealizedGain*, DirTotal*, rE*, AxialRatio, Polarization ratios and RCS quantities.

tools.name: SolutionData (expressions, primary_sweep_values, variations, active_variation, set_active_variation, intrinsics)
tools.description: The container returned by post.get_solution_data, setup.get_solution_data and report.get_solution_data: all traces of a report as arrays indexed by the primary sweep, for every variation solved. active_variation selects which variation the accessors return, primary_sweep_values gives the x axis, expressions the trace names, and the full_matrix_* properties expose everything at once (as pandas DataFrames when settings.enable_pandas_output is True).
tools.usage:
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data(expressions=["S(1,1)", "dB(S(2,1))"], setup_sweep_name=hfss.nominal_sweep)
data.expressions                # ['S(1,1)', 'dB(S(2,1))']
data.primary_sweep              # 'Freq'
data.primary_sweep_values       # list of floats
data.variations                 # list of variation dicts
data.active_variation           # current selection
data.set_active_variation(var_id=0)
data.intrinsics / data.intrinsics_by_variation(variation) / data.variation_values(variation)
data.nominal_variation
data.full_matrix_real_imag / data.full_matrix_mag_phase
data.is_real_only(expression=None)
data.units_sweeps / data.units_data (unit dictionaries)

parameters.name: set_active_variation(var_id)
parameters.description: Index into data.variations; subsequent get_expression_data/plot calls use it.

parameters.name: full_matrix_real_imag
parameters.description: Tuple (real, imag) of nested dicts/DataFrames covering all expressions and variations.

parameters.name: is_real_only
parameters.description: True when the expression has no imaginary part (e.g. dB values).

tools.example:
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data("S(1,1)", hfss.nominal_sweep, variations={"Freq": ["All"], "patch_l": ["All"]})
print(data.expressions, data.primary_sweep, len(data.primary_sweep_values))
for i, var in enumerate(data.variations):
    data.set_active_variation(i)
    mag = data.get_expression_data("S(1,1)", formula="mag")
    print(var, min(mag[1]))
tools.notes: Native: oModule("ReportSetup").GetSolutionDataPerVariation(reportType, solution, context, families, expressions) returning ISolutionDataResult objects with GetSweepValues/GetRealDataValues/GetImagDataValues. Older PyAEDT exposed data_real()/data_imag()/data_magnitude()/data_db20()/data_phase(); current releases use get_expression_data with a formula.

tools.name: SolutionData.get_expression_data / SolutionData.plot / plot_3d / export_data_to_csv
tools.description: Numeric and graphical access to a SolutionData: get_expression_data returns (x, y) lists for an expression after applying a formula (re, im, mag, db10, db20, phasedeg, phaserad, abs) for the active variation; plot draws one or more curves with matplotlib through the ReportPlotter (Cartesian or polar, with labels and an optional snapshot); plot_3d makes a 3D surface over primary and secondary sweeps; export_data_to_csv writes all data to CSV.
tools.usage:
x, y = data.get_expression_data(expression=None, formula=None, convert_to_SI=False)
plotter = data.plot(curves=None, formula=None, size=(1920, 1440), show_legend=True, x_label="", y_label="", title="",
                    snapshot_path=None, is_polar=False, show=True)
plotter = data.plot_3d(curve=None, primary_sweep="Theta", secondary_sweep="Phi", x_axis="Theta", y_axis="Phi", formula=None, ...)
data.export_data_to_csv(output, delimiter=";")
plotter = data.get_report_plotter(curves=None, formula=None, to_radians=False)

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Trace name; None uses the first expression.

parameters.name: formula
parameters.description: "re", "im", "mag"/"abs", "db10", "db20", "phasedeg", "phaserad"; None returns the real part.

parameters.name: curves
parameters.description: Expression(s) to plot; None plots the first.

parameters.name: snapshot_path
parameters.description: Save the matplotlib figure to this image path.

parameters.name: is_polar
parameters.description: Polar axes for pattern cuts (primary sweep in degrees).

tools.example:
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data("GainTotal", hfss.nominal_adaptive, report_category="Far Fields", context="3D",
                                   primary_sweep_variable="Theta",
                                   variations={"Freq": ["2.45GHz"], "Theta": ["All"], "Phi": ["0deg"]})
theta, gain_db = data.get_expression_data("GainTotal", formula="db10")
print(max(gain_db))
data.plot(formula="db10", is_polar=True, snapshot_path="C:/work/gain_cut.png", show=False)
data.export_data_to_csv("C:/work/gain_cut.csv", delimiter=",")

s = hfss.post.get_solution_data("S(1,1)")
f, s11_db = s.get_expression_data("S(1,1)", formula="db20")
tools.notes: Formulas are applied by PyAEDT on the complex data, so request the raw quantity ("S(1,1)") rather than "dB(S(1,1))" when several representations are needed. Plotting needs the [graphics]/[all] extras (matplotlib).

tools.name: SolutionData.ifft / ifft_to_file
tools.description: Inverse FFT of complex frequency-domain data along the primary sweep, turning a swept field or S-parameter into a time-domain response on the Python side: ifft returns the time series matrix, ifft_to_file writes one CSV per time step of a 2D field grid. It underpins time-gating, quick TDR-like views of a frequency sweep and animated time-domain field movies from a frequency-domain solve.
tools.usage:
t, y = data.ifft(curve_header="NearE", u_axis="_u", v_axis="_v", window=False)
folder = data.ifft_to_file(u_axis="_u", v_axis="_v", coord_system_center=None, db_val=False, num_frames=None, csv_path=None, name="res")

parameters.name: curve_header
parameters.description: Prefix of the expression columns to transform (e.g. "NearE" for NearEx/NearEy/NearEz).

parameters.name: u_axis / v_axis
parameters.description: Sweep variables that span the 2D grid (near-field rectangle U/V).

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Apply a window before the transform.

parameters.name: num_frames / db_val
parameters.description: Number of time frames to export and whether to write dB values.

tools.example:
nf = hfss.post.get_solution_data(["NearEx", "NearEy", "NearEz"], hfss.nominal_sweep, report_category="Near Fields",
                                 context="NF_plane", primary_sweep_variable="Freq",
                                 variations={"Freq": ["All"], "_u": ["All"], "_v": ["All"]})
folder = nf.ifft_to_file(u_axis="_u", v_axis="_v", num_frames=50, csv_path=hfss.working_directory, name="pulse")
hfss.post.plot_scene(frames=folder, output_gif_path="C:/work/pulse.gif", norm_index=0)
tools.notes: Requires a broadband sweep with enough points for the desired time window (dt = 1/BW, T = 1/df). The native Transient solver is the alternative when nonlinear or dispersive effects must be captured in time.

tools.name: hfss.post.get_solution_data_per_variation
tools.description: Low-level fetch that mirrors the native GetSolutionDataPerVariation call: a report category, a solution, a context list and a sweeps dictionary with the expressions to retrieve, returned as SolutionData. It is used when the higher-level get_solution_data guesses the wrong context or category (custom contexts for arrays, matrices, differential pairs, polylines).
tools.usage: data = hfss.post.get_solution_data_per_variation(solution_type="Far Fields", setup_sweep_name="", context=None, sweeps=None, expressions="")

parameters.name: solution_type
parameters.description: Report category string: "Modal Solution Data", "Terminal Solution Data", "Far Fields", "Fields", "Near Fields", "Eigenmode Parameters", "Antenna Parameters", "Emission Test".

parameters.name: setup_sweep_name
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1"; empty uses the nominal adaptive solution.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Native context array such as ["Context:=", "3D"] or ["Domain:=", "Sweep"].

parameters.name: sweeps
parameters.description: Families dict, default {"Theta": "All", "Phi": "All", "Freq": "All"}.

parameters.name: expressions
parameters.description: Trace expression(s).

tools.example:

print(fc.evaluate("V_feed", setup=hfss.nominal_adaptive, intrinsics={"Freq": "2.45GHz", "Phase": "0deg"}))

my_expr = {"name": "E2_surf", "description": "|E|^2 integrated on a sheet", "design_type": ["HFSS"],
           "fields_type": ["Fields"], "solution_type": "", "primary_sweep": "Freq", "assignment": "",
           "assignment_type": ["Surface"],
           "operations": ["Fundamental_Quantity('E')", "Operation('ComplexMag')", "Operation('Pow', 2)",
                          "EnterSurface('assignment')", "Operation('SurfaceValue')", "Operation('Integrate')"],
           "report": ["Data Table", "Rectangular Plot"]}
fc.add_expression(my_expr, "Aperture")
fc.expression_plot(my_expr, "Aperture", ["E2_surf"])
tools.notes: Named expressions are stored in the design and appear in Plot Fields and in report quantity lists under the Fields category (Calculator Expressions). Native: oModule("FieldsReporter").EnterQty(...), CalcOp(...), AddNamedExpression(name, "Fields"). The Advanced Fields Calculator extension offers the same catalog with a GUI.

tools.name: FieldExpressions builder (hfss.post.fields_calculator.expressions: scalar, vector, magnitude, dot, cross, integrate over Surface/Volume/Line)
tools.description: A typed, fluent builder for calculator expressions: start from a fundamental scalar or vector quantity (E, H, J, Poynting, named expressions, design variables, constants), chain algebraic and vector operations (magnitude, real/imag, conj, dot, cross, normal/tangent projections, sqrt, pow, ln, exp, trig) and finish with a domain aggregation (integrate, maximum, minimum, mean over a Surface, Volume or Line). The result is registered as a named expression, avoiding hand-written operation lists and stack errors.
tools.usage:
from ansys.aedt.core.visualization.post.field_calculator_expressions import Surface, Volume, Line, FieldExpressions
fx = hfss.post.fields_calculator.expressions      # FieldExpressions bound to the design's calculator
e = fx.vector("E", is_complex=True)
h = fx.vector("H", is_complex=True)
expr = (e.magnitude() * e.magnitude()).integrate(Surface("Aperture"))
poynt = e.cross(h.conj()).real().dot(fx.normal_vector()).integrate(Surface("RadSurf"))
# the built expression is then added to the calculator as a named expression (see notes)

parameters.name: fx.scalar(quantity, is_complex) / fx.vector(quantity, is_complex)
parameters.description: Fundamental quantities (E, H, Jvol, Jsurf, Poynting, Temp ...).

parameters.name: fx.scalar_constant / complex_constant / vector_constant / function(variable)
parameters.description: Constants and design-variable driven scalars.

parameters.name: fx.named_expression(name)
parameters.description: Reuse an existing named expression.

parameters.name: fx.normal_vector() / tangent_vector()
parameters.description: Geometry unit normal / tangent for flux and line integrals.

parameters.name: ScalarReal / ScalarComplex / VectorReal / VectorComplex
parameters.description: Result types with methods magnitude(), real(), imag(), conj(), phase(), dot(), cross(), integrate(domain), maximum(domain), minimum(domain), mean(domain), sqrt(), pow(), ln(), exp(), abs(), db().

parameters.name: Surface(name) / Volume(name) / Line(name)
parameters.description: Domains for the aggregations.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core.visualization.post.field_calculator_expressions import Surface, Line
fx = hfss.post.fields_calculator.expressions
e = fx.vector("E", is_complex=True)
v_line = e.real().dot(fx.tangent_vector()).integrate(Line("VLine"))      # voltage along a line
loss = fx.scalar("Ohmic_Loss").integrate(Surface("Patch"))               # conductor loss on a sheet
energy = (e.magnitude() * e.magnitude()).integrate(Surface("Aperture"))
print(v_line, loss, energy)   # each object renders the calculator operation sequence it represents
tools.notes: Introduced with the 1.x PyAEDT releases; the builder produces the same operation strings that the dictionary form of fields_calculator.add_expression accepts, and the 'Field expression builder' page of the user guide for the installed version documents how a built expression is registered as a named expression. Check hfss.post.fields_calculator.expression_names afterwards.

tools.name: hfss.post.ofieldsreporter / hfss.post.oreportsetup (native module handles for calculator and report scripting)
tools.description: Direct handles to the native FieldsReporter and ReportSetup modules from the post-processor, for stack-based calculator sequences and report calls that PyAEDT does not wrap: EnterQty/EnterVol/EnterSurf/EnterLine/EnterScalar/CalcOp/ClcEval/AddNamedExpression/ExportOnGrid on ofieldsreporter, and CreateReport/AddTraces/ExportToFile/CreateOutputVariable-style calls on oreportsetup. Recorded GUI scripts paste in unchanged.
tools.usage:
ofr = hfss.post.ofieldsreporter          # == hfss.get_module("FieldsReporter")
ors = hfss.post.oreportsetup             # == hfss.get_module("ReportSetup")
ofr.EnterQty("Poynting"); ofr.CalcOp("Real"); ofr.EnterSurf("RadSurf"); ofr.CalcOp("Normal"); ofr.CalcOp("Integrate")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("Prad", "Fields")
ofr.ClcEval("Setup1 : LastAdaptive", ["Freq:=", "2.45GHz", "Phase:=", "0deg"])
value = ofr.GetTopEntryValue("Setup1 : LastAdaptive", ["Freq:=", "2.45GHz", "Phase:=", "0deg"])

parameters.name: Stack operations
parameters.description: CalcStack("push"/"pop"/"clear"/"exch"/"rlup"/"rldn"), ClearAllNamedExpr(), CopyNamedExprToStack(name), DeleteNamedExpr(name).

parameters.name: CalcOp names
parameters.description: Mag, ComplexMag, Real, Imag, Phase, Conj, Smooth, Normal, Tangent, Dot, Cross, Integrate, Maximum, Minimum, Mean, Value, dB, +, -, *, /, Sqrt, Pow, Exp, Ln, Abs, Grad, Div, Curl, ScalarX/Y/Z, VecX/Y/Z, Domain, AtPhase, AtTime, Derivative.

parameters.name: GetTopEntryValue
parameters.description: Evaluates the top of the stack and returns the value as a list of strings.

tools.example:
ofr = hfss.post.ofieldsreporter
ofr.CalcStack("clear")
ofr.EnterQty("E")
ofr.CalcOp("ComplexMag")
ofr.EnterVol("Sub")
ofr.CalcOp("Maximum")
ofr.AddNamedExpression("Emax_sub", "Fields")
val = ofr.GetTopEntryValue(hfss.nominal_adaptive, ["Freq:=", "2.45GHz", "Phase:=", "0deg"])
print(float(val[0]))

ors = hfss.post.oreportsetup
ors.CreateReport("Emax vs f", "Fields", "Rectangular Plot", hfss.nominal_sweep, ["Domain:=", "Sweep"],
                 ["Freq:=", ["All"], "Phase:=", ["0deg"]], ["X Component:=", "Freq", "Y Component:=", ["Emax_sub"]])
tools.notes: The calculator is stateful: always clear the stack before a sequence and after AddNamedExpression. Named expressions defined natively are visible to hfss.post.fields_calculator.expression_names and usable in create_report with report_category="Fields".

tools.name: hfss.get_antenna_data / FfdSolutionDataExporter (far-field export with metadata)
tools.description: Export the far fields of every port (embedded element patterns) for chosen frequencies on an infinite sphere to .ffd files plus a JSON metadata file describing ports, frequencies, geometry and power, and return an exporter whose farfield_data attribute is an FfdSolutionData ready for beamforming, cuts and 3D plots. With link_to_hfss=False the same data is read back from the files without AEDT, which is the basis of array post-processing in Python.
tools.usage:
ffd = hfss.get_antenna_data(frequencies=None, setup=None, sphere=None, variations=None, overwrite=True, link_to_hfss=True,
                            export_touchstone=True, set_phase_center_per_port=True)
ffd.metadata_file / ffd.farfield_data / ffd.incident_power
hfss.export_element_pattern(frequencies, setup, sphere, variations=None, element_name="element", output_dir=None)
hfss.export_antenna_metadata(frequencies, setup, sphere, variations=None, output_dir=None, export_element_pattern=True, export_objects=True, export_touchstone=True, export_power=True)

parameters.name: frequencies
parameters.description: Float, list, or None for all solved frequencies of the setup (numbers in Hz or strings with units).

parameters.name: setup / sphere
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" (or LastAdaptive) and the infinite sphere name; a sphere is created if None.

parameters.name: variations
parameters.description: Variation dict; nominal when None.

parameters.name: link_to_hfss
parameters.description: True returns FfdSolutionDataExporter bound to the design; False returns a standalone FfdSolutionData from the exported files.

parameters.name: export_touchstone / set_phase_center_per_port
parameters.description: Also export the S-matrix (for accepted power) and set port phase centres.

tools.example:
hfss.insert_infinite_sphere(name="3D", x_step=2, y_step=2)
hfss.analyze()
ffd = hfss.get_antenna_data(frequencies=[2.45e9], setup=hfss.nominal_sweep, sphere="3D")
print(ffd.metadata_file)
data = ffd.farfield_data
print(data.frequencies, data.all_element_names, data.radiated_power)
data.plot_cut(quantity="RealizedGain", primary_sweep="theta", secondary_sweep_value=[0, 90], quantity_format="dB10")
tools.notes: Native: oModule("RadField").ExportRadiationFieldsToFile(...) per port plus PyAEDT-written JSON. Each port is excited alone (others matched) so the files contain embedded element patterns; combine_farfield applies weights afterwards.

tools.name: FfdSolutionData (plot_cut, plot_contour, plot_3d, combine_farfield, farfield_data, radiated_power, accepted_power, phase/magnitude weights)
tools.description: Standalone far-field post-processor working on exported .ffd data: select the frequency, set per-port magnitude and phase weights or a scan direction (theta_scan/phi_scan with taper), combine the element patterns into the array pattern, and plot 2D cuts, contour maps or interactive 3D patterns over the geometry with PyVista/matplotlib. It also reports incident, accepted and radiated power per element and in total, and exposes the raw pattern arrays for custom processing.
tools.usage:
from ansys.aedt.core.visualization.advanced.farfield_visualization import FfdSolutionData
data = FfdSolutionData(input_file, frequency=None, variation=None, model_info=None, incident_power=None, touchstone_file=None)
data.frequency = 2.45e9
data.magnitude = {"P1": 1, "P2": 1}; data.phase = {"P1": 0, "P2": 90}
data.theta_scan = 30; data.phi_scan = 0; data.taper = "flat"   # or "cosine", "triangular", "hamming"
ff = data.combine_farfield(phi_scan=0, theta_scan=0)
data.farfield_data          # dict of arrays: rETheta, rEPhi, rETotal, Gain*, RealizedGain*, Directivity*, Theta, Phi
data.plot_cut(quantity="RealizedGain", primary_sweep="theta", secondary_sweep_value=0, phi=0, theta=0, title="", quantity_format="dB10", output_file=None, show=True, is_polar=False, show_legend=True)
data.plot_contour(quantity="RealizedGain", phi=0, theta=0, title="", quantity_format="dB10", output_file=None, show=True, polar=False, max_theta=180, levels=64)
data.plot_3d(quantity="RealizedGain", phi=0, theta=0, quantity_format="dB10", output_file=None, show=True, show_geometry=True, background=None, rotation=None)
data.plot_3d_chart(quantity="RealizedGain", ...)
data.get_far_field_mesh(quantity="RealizedGain", quantity_format="dB10")
data.radiated_power / data.accepted_power / data.incident_power / *_element / data.active_s_parameters

parameters.name: input_file
parameters.description: The JSON metadata file written by get_antenna_data (pyaedt_antenna_metadata.json).

parameters.name: quantity
parameters.description: "rETheta", "rEPhi", "rETotal", "GainTotal", "RealizedGainTotal", "Directivity", "AxialRatio"... (check data.farfield_data.keys()).

parameters.name: quantity_format
parameters.description: "dB10", "dB20", "abs", "real", "imag", "phase".

parameters.name: primary_sweep / secondary_sweep_value
parameters.description: "theta" or "phi" as the x axis, and the fixed value(s) of the other angle.

parameters.name: magnitude / phase / taper / theta_scan / phi_scan
parameters.description: Array weights: explicit per-port dicts, or a scan direction with an amplitude taper.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core.visualization.advanced.farfield_visualization import FfdSolutionData
data = FfdSolutionData("C:/work/ffd/pyaedt_antenna_metadata.json")
data.frequency = data.frequencies[0]
data.theta_scan = 20; data.phi_scan = 0; data.taper = "cosine"
data.plot_cut("RealizedGain", primary_sweep="theta", secondary_sweep_value=[0, 90], quantity_format="dB10",
              is_polar=True, output_file="C:/work/cuts.png", show=False)
data.plot_3d("RealizedGain", show_geometry=True, output_file="C:/work/pattern3d.png", show=False)
print("Prad =", data.radiated_power, "W; Pacc =", data.accepted_power, "W")
tools.notes: Works without a license or AEDT once the files exist - the basis of the Array Post-Processing example and of the antenna-array toolkit. Element patterns are embedded (mutual coupling included) because each port was solved with the others matched; the combination is exact for the solved element positions.

tools.name: hfss.get_rcs_data / MonostaticRCSExporter (monostatic RCS export and plotting)
tools.description: Export monostatic radar cross section results (ComplexMonostaticRCSTheta/Phi over the incident-angle sweep of a plane-wave excitation) for chosen frequencies to an HDF5/JSON dataset with metadata, and return an exporter whose rcs_data gives access to the MonostaticRCSData/Plotter classes for angular cuts, 2D maps, range profiles, ISAR images and waterfall plots computed in Python from the exported data.
tools.usage:
rcs = hfss.get_rcs_data(frequencies=None, setup=None, expression="ComplexMonostaticRCSTheta", variations=None, overwrite=True,
                        link_to_hfss=True, variation_name=None)
rcs.metadata_file / rcs.rcs_data
plotter = rcs.rcs_data.plotter   # MonostaticRCSPlotter: plot_rcs(), plot_range_profile(), plot_waterfall(), plot_isar_2d(), plot_scene()

parameters.name: frequencies
parameters.description: Hz floats or strings with units; None = all solved frequencies.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" or LastAdaptive.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: "ComplexMonostaticRCSTheta" or "ComplexMonostaticRCSPhi" (co-/cross-polar components).

parameters.name: link_to_hfss
parameters.description: False returns only the metadata path for offline processing.

parameters.name: variation_name
parameters.description: Label for the exported variation folder.

tools.example:
hfss = Hfss(project="C:/work/rcs_target.aedt", solution_type="SBR+")
hfss.plane_wave(vector_format="Spherical", polarization="Vertical", propagation_vector=[["0deg", "180deg", 181], ["90deg", "90deg", 1]])
hfss.create_setup("SBR1", setup_type="HFSSSBR", RangeStart="9GHz", RangeEnd="11GHz", RangeStep="0.05GHz")
hfss.analyze()
rcs = hfss.get_rcs_data(setup="SBR1 : Sweep", expression="ComplexMonostaticRCSTheta", variation_name="vv")
print(rcs.metadata_file)
rcs.rcs_data.plotter.plot_rcs(primary_sweep="IWavePhi", secondary_sweep_value=90, show=False, output_file="C:/work/rcs.png")
tools.notes: Monostatic RCS requires a plane wave with an angular sweep (the incident direction becomes the IWaveTheta/IWavePhi sweeps) in Far Fields reports; SBR+ is the usual solver for electrically large targets, FEM with FE-BI for small ones. Bistatic RCS is reported directly from Far Fields (RCSTotal/Theta/Phi vs Theta/Phi).

tools.name: hfss.get_touchstone_data / TouchstoneData (scikit-rf based Touchstone post-processing)
tools.description: Read the solved S-matrix as a TouchstoneData object (a scikit-rf Network subclass) either straight from the design or from an .sNp file, and analyse it in Python: plot insertion/return losses and crosstalk, find the worst curve against a limit, convert to mixed-mode with a given port ordering, reduce the port set, and use every scikit-rf method (renormalize, time-domain, cascading). It complements export_touchstone for scripts that post-process channel results.
tools.usage:
ts = hfss.get_touchstone_data(setup=None, sweep=None, variations=None)     # list of TouchstoneData, one per variation
from ansys.aedt.core.visualization.advanced.touchstone_parser import TouchstoneData
ts = TouchstoneData(touchstone_file="C:/work/board.s8p")
ts.plot_insertion_losses(threshold=-3, plot=True)
ts.plot_return_losses(threshold=-10, plot=True)
ts.plot_next_xtalk(threshold=-40, plot=True) / ts.plot_fext_xtalk(threshold=-40, plot=True)
ts.get_return_loss_index(excitation_name_prefix="") / get_insertion_loss_index(threshold=-3)
ts.get_worst_curve(freq_min=None, freq_max=None, worst_is_higher=True, curve_list=None, plot=True)
ts.get_mixed_mode_touchstone_data(num_of_diff_ports=None, port_ordering="1234")
ts.reduce(ports)
ts.port_names / ts.s / ts.f / ts.frequency   # scikit-rf attributes

parameters.name: setup / sweep / variations
parameters.description: Solution to read from the design; all variations are returned as a list.

parameters.name: touchstone_file
parameters.description: Path of an .sNp file (Touchstone 1.0 or 2.0).

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Limit in dB used to colour/flag curves in the plots and indices.

parameters.name: port_ordering
parameters.description: "1234" or "1324" pairing convention for mixed-mode conversion.

tools.example:
ts_list = hfss.get_touchstone_data(setup="Setup1", sweep="Sweep1")
ts = ts_list[0]
print(ts.port_names, ts.f[:3])
worst = ts.get_worst_curve(freq_min=1e9, freq_max=10e9, worst_is_higher=False, curve_list=ts.get_insertion_loss_index(), plot=False)
mm = ts.get_mixed_mode_touchstone_data(port_ordering="1324")
mm.write_touchstone("C:/work/board_mixed.s4p")
tools.notes: Requires scikit-rf (pyaedt[all]). The same class powers the Circuit create_touchstone_report helpers; the raw native export remains oModule("Solutions").ExportNetworkData.

tools.name: hfss.set_export_touchstone (Touchstone export options: format, passivity, causality, renormalization, precision)

hfss.set_export_touchstone(file_format="TouchStone1.0", enforce_passivity=True, enforce_causality=False, use_common_ground=True,
                           show_gamma_comments=True, renormalize=False, impedance=50.0, fitting_error=0.5, maximum_poles=1000,

                           relative_error_tolerance=True, ensure_accurate_fit=False, touchstone_output="MA", units="GHz", precision=11)

parameters.name: file_format

parameters.name: enforce_passivity / passivity_type / enforce_causality

parameters.name: fitting_error / maximum_poles / column_fitting_type / state_space_fitting / ensure_accurate_fit

parameters.name: renormalize / impedance
parameters.description: Renormalise all ports to a real impedance.

parameters.name: touchstone_output / units / precision

hfss.set_export_touchstone(file_format="TouchStone2.0", enforce_passivity=True, enforce_causality=True,

hfss.plot(objects=None, show=True, export_path=None, ...)

tools.name: hfss.create_scattering / hfss.get_traces_for_plot / hfss.create_q_factor_report / hfss.get_next_xtalk_list / get_fext_xtalk_list
tools.description: Report shortcuts on the Hfss object: create_scattering builds the standard S-parameter plot for all ports (or given ones) of a sweep, get_traces_for_plot assembles expression lists filtered by port name patterns and a category (S, Y, Z, VSWR...), create_q_factor_report exports the eigenmode Q table as CSV, and the crosstalk helpers list near-end / far-end coupling expressions between driver and receiver ports for SI reports.
tools.usage:
hfss.create_scattering(plot="S Parameter Plot Nominal", sweep=None, ports=None, ports_excited=None, variations=None)
traces = hfss.get_traces_for_plot(get_self_terms=True, get_mutual_terms=True, first_element_filter=None, second_element_filter=None, category="dB(S", differential_pairs=None)
hfss.create_q_factor_report(setup=None, output_file=None)
hfss.get_next_xtalk_list(trlist=None, tx_prefix="", rx_prefix="", math_formula="") / hfss.get_fext_xtalk_list(...)

parameters.name: ports / ports_excited
parameters.description: Receiving and exciting port subsets for create_scattering (None = all).

parameters.name: first_element_filter / second_element_filter
parameters.description: Wildcards on the two S indices, e.g. "P1*" and "*".

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Prefix such as "dB(S", "S", "VSWR(", "Y(", "Z(".

parameters.name: tx_prefix / rx_prefix / math_formula
parameters.description: Port-name prefixes identifying drivers and receivers, and the wrapping function ("dB").

tools.example:
hfss.create_scattering("All S", sweep=hfss.nominal_sweep)
traces = hfss.get_traces_for_plot(get_self_terms=False, get_mutual_terms=True, first_element_filter="P1*", category="dB(S")
hfss.post.create_report(traces, plot_name="Coupling from P1")

hfss.post.create_report(next_, plot_name="NEXT")
tools.notes: In Modal designs traces refer to port modes (S(P1:1,P2:1)); in Terminal designs to terminal names. create_q_factor_report only applies to Eigenmode designs.
